notes:
Topline: federal defense archive use-case — secure, air-gapped RAG + reranking. Customer runs historical intelligence archives (approx 1.2B documents, mixed binary/text, many scanned PDFs) and needs vectorized search + reranking pipeline that can operate in an air-gapped on-prem env. Primary ask: turnkey on-prem installer, KMS/HSM integration, and a closed-network POC that mimics production scale.

Key technical constraints:
- Indexing/scale: ~1B+ vectors, shard/replica strategy, efficient cold storage for archival docs, snapshot/import tooling for air-gapped infra.
- Latency targets: tail latency for top-k candidate retrieval + neural reranker <= 300ms (goal 150-200ms) for 99th pct under 100 qps; 200-500 qps bursts acceptable with dedicated capacity.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement team pushing for cost-per-query < $0.02 for routine archival lookups; reranking-heavy queries allowed higher cost but must be predictable.
- Model preferences: open models (LLaMA-family variants) or gov-approved models; quantized 8-bit / int4 options desired; ability to pin model versions and fall back to cheaper reranker.
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, audit trails on every query, KMS integration for key escrow, immutable logs for e-discovery. Must pass internal STIG review.

Customer quotes / call notes:
- "We cannot have any egress — installer must run in their MAAS environment and accept sealed media for transfer." - SecOps lead.
- "If you can show a deterministic per-query cost model and a compact on-disk index, procurement will move faster." - Procurement director.

Recent timeline: see recent_activities for details. POC status: architecture workshop done; dataset ingest dry-run completed in staging (offline); reranker performance baseline measured on 5M doc subset (recall + nDCG reported). Security questionnaire answered, but STIG remediation plan pending.

Notes on commercial/procurement: They require a NTE (not-to-exceed) pricing line in SOW for first-year reserved capacity + air-gap integration fees. Legal wants liability language for on-prem installs. Typical procurement cycles — expect 60-90 day negotiation post final SOW.

Stitched asks for Redwood: air-gapped installer + offline telemetry options; detailed on-disk index size per 1M vectors under quantized profile; recommended GPU count for 99th pct 100 qps target; fallback strategy when dedicated pool saturated; sample SOW language for integration with government networks.

use_case_summary: Government archive search: enable secure RAG workflows across classified corpora. System must support large-scale vector index (1B+ vectors), deterministic per-query costs, and neural reranking within strict latency SLOs. Primary outcomes: fast, auditable search for analysts; offline deployability for air-gapped environments; producible SOW for procurement.
procurement_notes: Requires CAGE/DoD contract clauses; will request SOW + MSA redlines. Integration window contingent on security sprint (STIG remediation). PO expected from central contracting office; expect 60-90 day approval. Budgeting prefers fixed-price first-year + usage ceiling.
technical_risks: Index storage footprint higher than expected for full-fidelity vectors — need quantization plan; reranker model memory pressure may push multi-GPU serving; offline ingestion for 1B docs will require custom chunked transfer and retry semantics.
